games.name: Red Dead Redemption 2
games.award_evidence: The Game Awards' official 2018 winner video names Red Dead Redemption 2 Best Narrative.

mechanics.name: Living open world
mechanics.detail: Ride, hunt, fish, trade and discover changing frontier encounters across a large connected map.

mechanics.name: Camp relationships
mechanics.detail: Arthur's camp is a social base where chores, conversations and companion stories develop over time.

mechanics.name: Honor and choice
mechanics.detail: Player conduct changes encounters and the tone of Arthur's journey.

games.return_reason: The frontier supports deliberate wandering, optional stories and a strong sense of place; returning can mean finishing camp threads, hunting a missing species or replaying missions with different honor choices.
games.allworld_transfer: Use neighborhoods as readable social ecologies: residents remember help or harm, homes and work sites become visible progress, and exploration unlocks relationships, careers and collectible histories.
games.risk: Pacing and cinematic commitment may feel slow; avoid copying its violence or assuming a single protagonist arc.
games.retention_type: campaign continuation, exploration and collection completion

games.name: Grand Theft Auto V
games.award_evidence: Xbox Wire's official VGX 2013 results name Grand Theft Auto V Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Three protagonists
mechanics.detail: Switch between Michael, Franklin and Trevor to experience linked missions from different viewpoints.

mechanics.name: Heist planning
mechanics.detail: Major scores combine preparation, crew selection and branching approach choices.

mechanics.name: Open-world activities
mechanics.detail: Driving, flying, shooting, property ownership and side activities fill Los Santos beyond the main plot.

games.return_reason: Role switching and heist variants create replayable routes, while the open city offers short self-directed sessions; GTA Online adds a continuing social layer distinct from the finished campaign.
games.allworld_transfer: Give residents complementary roles in a city operation, let players plan missions with AI or human crews, and make properties, jobs and public reputation persist visibly across neighborhoods.
games.risk: Crime fantasy and satire may not fit every Allworld audience; keep civic missions and consequences legible.
games.retention_type: campaign replay plus ongoing social sandbox

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
games.award_evidence: Nintendo's 8 December 2017 Game Awards recap states Breath of the Wild won Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Physics-driven exploration
mechanics.detail: Climb, glide, cook and combine objects to solve problems in many viable ways.

mechanics.name: Shrines and discovery
mechanics.detail: Short puzzle spaces and landmarks create frequent self-directed goals.

mechanics.name: Environmental survival
mechanics.detail: Temperature, weather, food and equipment shape route planning.

games.return_reason: Curiosity drives return: players notice a distant landmark, test a new combination or revisit a blocked route with new equipment. Completion is self-paced rather than calendar-driven.
games.allworld_transfer: Build cities with layered affordances: rooftops, weather, tools and local knowledge should open multiple routes, while discoveries become map annotations, resident stories and visible civic improvements.
games.risk: Systemic freedom can reduce authored narrative focus; provide clear onboarding and strong local goals.

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

award.name: Japan Game Awards 2024
award.category: Grand Award / Award for Excellence / Best Sales Award

games.award_evidence: CESA's official 2024 results name Tears of the Kingdom the Grand Award, Award for Excellence and Best Sales Award recipient.

mechanics.name: Ultrahand construction
mechanics.detail: Attach objects to build vehicles, tools and machines for traversal and puzzles.

mechanics.name: Three-layer world
mechanics.detail: Sky islands, surface regions and the Depths create vertical exploration loops.

mechanics.name: Fuse and Ascend
mechanics.detail: Weapons gain situational properties and players can pass through ceilings to reframe routes.

games.return_reason: Construction creates expressive mastery: a player returns to redesign a vehicle, solve a puzzle differently or finish an unexplored layer. The strongest pull is project-based, not daily obligation.
games.allworld_transfer: Let players and AI residents co-build homes, transit and businesses from local materials; record blueprints, ownership and community use as visible accomplishments.
games.risk: A deep toolset can overwhelm newcomers and produce exploits that bypass social goals.

games.name: God of War (2018)
games.award_evidence: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' 2019 results name God of War Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Leviathan Axe combat
mechanics.detail: Throwing, recalling and upgrading the axe makes positioning part of every fight.

mechanics.name: Companion combat
mechanics.detail: Atreus provides ranged support and grows as the father-son relationship develops.

mechanics.name: Norse exploration
mechanics.detail: The journey combines combat, exploration and optional favors across Norse realms.

games.return_reason: The return impulse is relational and mastery-based: players revisit optional favors, test upgraded builds and see how a shared journey changes its characters.
games.allworld_transfer: Make AI companions remember promises and develop skills, with homes, family spaces and completed favors showing relationship history in the world.
games.risk: A tightly authored, linear emotional arc may limit persistent simulation; use relationship beats as optional local stories.

games.name: God of War Ragnarök
games.award_evidence: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' 2023 winners announcement names God of War Ragnarök Adventure Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Realm-hopping exploration
mechanics.detail: Nine realms combine authored quests, traversal puzzles and optional favors.

mechanics.name: Weapon and skill builds
mechanics.detail: Axe, blades, shield and companion abilities support different combat approaches.

mechanics.name: Character relationship quests
mechanics.detail: Party members' personal goals unfold through dialogue and side missions.

games.return_reason: Post-campaign exploration, build experimentation and unresolved companion favors give players reasons to continue after the central story, while completionists can chase collectibles.
games.allworld_transfer: Represent cities as linked districts with resident-led favors, evolving skills and remembered family ties; completed quests should alter spaces and available conversations.
games.risk: Large authored content volume can create scope and localization costs.
games.retention_type: campaign continuation, side-quest completion and mastery

games.name: The Last of Us (2013)
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2014 winners release names The Last of Us the Best Game winner.

mechanics.name: Stealth and resource scarcity
mechanics.detail: Players scout threats, craft limited tools and choose when to fight or evade.

mechanics.name: Companion traversal
mechanics.detail: Ellie and other companions participate in encounters and environmental problem solving.

mechanics.name: Environmental storytelling
mechanics.detail: Spaces, notes and quiet interactions reveal history beyond exposition.

games.return_reason: Its primary return is campaign continuation and replay for higher difficulty, alternate stealth routes and emotional re-reading; it is not designed as a daily live service.
games.allworld_transfer: Use scarce resources, trusted companions and layered environmental clues to make neighborhoods feel inhabited; resident memories can turn exploration into relationship discovery.
games.risk: Dark survival themes and scarcity may exhaust players; provide gentler city stories and accessibility options.

games.name: The Last of Us Part II
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2021 winners release names The Last of Us Part II the EE Game of the Year winner.

mechanics.name: Stealth sandbox
mechanics.detail: Tall grass, prone movement, sound cues and enemy flanking create multiple encounter solutions.

mechanics.name: Crafting and upgrades
mechanics.detail: Scavenged materials support weapons, skills and risk-reward loadouts.

mechanics.name: Perspective shift
mechanics.detail: Playable characters expose different abilities, spaces and interpretations of the same conflict.

games.return_reason: Players return for alternate combat approaches, collectible completion and replay that recontextualizes relationships; its retention is primarily narrative and mastery-led.
games.allworld_transfer: Let residents hold competing memories of a city event, with skills, inventory and relationships changing what each player can discover.
games.risk: Perspective reversals can confuse social simulation if causality is not clearly surfaced.
games.retention_type: campaign continuation, replay mastery and collection

games.name: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2017 winners release names Uncharted 4: A Thief's End the Best Game winner.

mechanics.name: Traversal set pieces
mechanics.detail: Climbing, rope swinging, driving and swimming turn cinematic spaces into playable routes.

mechanics.name: Cover shooting
mechanics.detail: Readable arenas support movement, stealth openings and direct firefights.

mechanics.name: Partner banter
mechanics.detail: Companions comment on locations and actions, reinforcing a traveling group dynamic.

games.return_reason: The campaign is a polished authored trip; replay comes from missed treasures, speed or higher difficulty rather than indefinite daily activity.
games.allworld_transfer: Create expedition missions where residents provide context, banter and optional routes; discoveries can become museum pieces, maps and local reputation.
games.risk: Set-piece spectacle is expensive and less reusable than systemic simulation.

games.name: Ghost of Tsushima
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2021 winners release names Ghost of Tsushima the Audio Achievement winner.

mechanics.name: Stance-based swordplay
mechanics.detail: Different stances answer enemy archetypes and reward learning readable counters.

mechanics.name: Guiding wind exploration
mechanics.detail: Wind, foxes and birds direct players toward points of interest without a cluttered map.

mechanics.name: charms and cosmetics
mechanics.detail: Combat upgrades and visual collections make exploration legible and expressive.

games.return_reason: Aesthetic exploration, duel mastery and collectible completion invite long sessions and later revisits; the core story still has a clear ending.
games.allworld_transfer: Use sound, weather and resident signals to guide exploration through culturally specific neighborhoods; visible clothing, homes and civic landmarks can record earned status.
games.risk: Historical imitation can flatten cultures if treated as decoration; consult local context and avoid genericized heritage.

games.name: Horizon Zero Dawn
games.award_evidence: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' 2018 results name Horizon Zero Dawn the Outstanding Technical Achievement winner.

mechanics.name: Machine hunting
mechanics.detail: Scan machine weaknesses and use elemental arrows, traps and terrain to dismantle parts.

mechanics.name: Open-world quests
mechanics.detail: Main quests, errands, ruins and settlements combine exploration with character stories.

mechanics.name: Skill and gear progression
mechanics.detail: Aloy unlocks abilities and modifies weapons for different hunt styles.

games.return_reason: The scan-plan-execute loop creates mastery, while new machines and lore sites make future expeditions meaningful. Returns are mostly quest, hunt and completion driven.
games.allworld_transfer: Give each district readable resource ecologies and AI residents with jobs, tools and vulnerabilities; player knowledge should improve both mission planning and civic care.
games.risk: Combat complexity and lore volume can make onboarding heavy.

games.name: Death Stranding
games.award_evidence: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' 2020 results name Death Stranding the Outstanding Technical Achievement winner.

mechanics.name: Delivery planning
mechanics.detail: Balance cargo, terrain, weather and equipment while transporting packages between shelters.

mechanics.name: Asynchronous structures
mechanics.detail: Players build roads, bridges, signs and generators that others can use.

mechanics.name: Connection network
mechanics.detail: Unlocking isolated facilities expands the shared map and rewards mutual aid.

games.return_reason: The distinctive return loop is route optimization and helping strangers indirectly; campaign chapters remain authored, but shared infrastructure gives exploration a continuing social purpose.
games.allworld_transfer: Make player-built paths, shelters and services materially useful to AI residents and other players, with attribution and maintenance creating visible civic legacy.
games.risk: Asynchronous systems need clear consent, moderation and anti-griefing rules.
games.retention_type: campaign continuation plus asynchronous social contribution

games.name: Control
games.award_evidence: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences' 2020 results name Control Action Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Telekinetic combat
mechanics.detail: Jesse combines weapon forms with launch, shield and evade powers in destructible spaces.

mechanics.name: Metroidvania investigation
mechanics.detail: Access cards and abilities reopen the shifting Oldest House for secrets and side missions.

mechanics.name: Mod and upgrade builds
mechanics.detail: Personal and weapon mods tune survivability, damage and preferred play patterns.

games.return_reason: Returning means experimenting with powers, clearing optional alerts and revisiting spaces with new abilities; its surreal setting rewards close reading and mastery.
games.allworld_transfer: Use mutable buildings, unexplained civic systems and resident investigations to make neighborhoods feel discoverable; upgrades can reveal new social and career pathways.
games.risk: Surreal ambiguity can obscure goals; pair mystery with strong wayfinding and readable consequences.
games.retention_type: mastery, investigation and optional mission completion

games.name: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice

award.name: Japan Game Awards
award.category: Award for Excellence (Games of the Year Division)

games.award_evidence: CESA's official 2019 results name Sekiro an Award for Excellence recipient in the Games of the Year Division.

mechanics.name: Deflection posture combat
mechanics.detail: Timed parries and pressure break enemy posture, making fights a rhythm of attack and defense.

mechanics.name: Grappling and vertical traversal
mechanics.detail: A prosthetic arm opens rooftops, ambushes and alternate routes through Sengoku spaces.

mechanics.name: Resurrection and prosthetics
mechanics.detail: Death can be strategically delayed, while tools and skill upgrades support different encounters.

games.return_reason: Its strongest return driver is mastery: players retry bosses, learn timing and pursue alternate endings. This is deliberate practice, not daily-service retention.
games.allworld_transfer: Create optional skill schools, visible mastery badges and mentor relationships where residents teach techniques that change how missions can be solved.
games.risk: High difficulty may exclude broad audiences; offer accessibility tuning without removing meaningful mastery.

games.name: Dark Souls III

award.name: Japan Game Awards
award.category: Award for Excellence (Games of the Year Division)

games.award_evidence: CESA's official 2016 results name Dark Souls III an Award for Excellence recipient in the Games of the Year Division.

mechanics.name: Risk-and-recovery combat
mechanics.detail: Death drops souls at the failure point, creating a recover-or-lose tension loop.

mechanics.name: Build and equipment choices
mechanics.detail: Stats, weapons, armor and spells support distinct character approaches.

mechanics.name: Interconnected world
mechanics.detail: Shortcuts, hidden areas and environmental clues reward careful mapping.

games.return_reason: Players return to improve routes, recover lost resources, try new builds and complete optional areas; community knowledge also makes discoveries shareable.
games.allworld_transfer: Make city mastery legible through maps, shortcuts, local mentors and recoverable setbacks; visible build choices can shape careers and missions.
games.risk: Punishment without clear feedback can feel hostile; protect experimentation with readable stakes and recovery options.

games.name: Bloodborne
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2016 winners release names Bloodborne the Game Design winner.

mechanics.name: Aggressive rally combat
mechanics.detail: Recent damage can be recovered by counterattacking, rewarding forward pressure.

mechanics.name: Trick weapons
mechanics.detail: Transforming weapons switch move sets and range mid-fight.

mechanics.name: Layered gothic investigation
mechanics.detail: Shortcuts, chalice dungeons and environmental clues connect combat to world discovery.

games.return_reason: The return loop is learning enemy patterns, refining weapon timing and uncovering optional layers; chalice dungeons extend experimentation beyond the campaign.
games.allworld_transfer: Translate rally into social recovery: residents can repair standing through helpful action, while transformed tools and hidden civic layers reward revisiting familiar streets.
games.risk: Gothic horror and opaque quest logic need audience controls and clearer optional guidance.
games.retention_type: mastery, investigation and optional dungeon completion
